patterns.title: Two Pointers
patterns.description: Move multiple indices together to replace nested loops with linear scans.
patterns.explanation: Used when multiple indices move together to reduce nested loops. Mostly appears in sorted arrays, in-place modification, pair problems, and window movement.

problems.title: Move Zeroes

notes.intuition: Keep a write pointer for the next non-zero value and scan once with a read pointer.
notes.whyPattern: The read pointer discovers useful values while the write pointer marks where they belong.
mistakes: Changing the relative order of non-zero values

problems.approach: Scan the array. Whenever a non-zero value is found, swap it with the value at the write pointer and advance the write pointer.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array

notes.intuition: A sorted array groups duplicates, so only the first value of each group must be written.
notes.whyPattern: One pointer reads every value and the other maintains the compact unique prefix.
mistakes: Forgetting to return the unique length

problems.approach: Start the write pointer at one. For every new value different from the previous value, write it into the compact prefix.

problems.title: Two Sum II

notes.intuition: In a sorted array, moving left increases the sum and moving right decreases it.
notes.whyPattern: Two pointers allow deterministic movement based on whether the current sum is too small or too large.
mistakes: Using hash map despite sorted input
Returning zero-based indices on one-based platforms

problems.approach: Place pointers at both ends. Compare their sum to target and move the pointer that can bring the sum closer.

patterns.title: Prefix Sum + Hashing
patterns.description: Store cumulative values to answer range and subarray questions quickly.
patterns.explanation: Use prefix sums when a subarray property can be expressed as the difference between two cumulative states.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K

notes.intuition: If current prefix is p, a previous prefix p - k creates a subarray with sum k.
notes.whyPattern: Hashing stores how many previous prefixes can pair with the current one.
mistakes: Using sliding window when negatives exist
Forgetting the initial prefix sum zero

problems.approach: Track prefix sum frequencies. At each index, add the count of previous prefixes that would produce k.

patterns.title: Kadane
patterns.description: Carry the best subarray ending at the current index.
patterns.explanation: Kadane works when every step decides whether to extend the previous segment or start fresh.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray

notes.intuition: A negative running contribution should be dropped before starting a better subarray.
notes.whyPattern: The best subarray ending here only depends on the previous best ending and the current value.

problems.approach: For each value, choose between starting a new subarray and extending the previous one.
